summary: Anthropic published an analysis mapping 832 accounts banned for malicious cyber activity over a year onto the MITRE ATT&CK framework, describing how attackers use AI in later, more autonomous stages of cyberattacks and where the framework fails to capture this behavior.

practices.reason: The risk-scoring methodology and its finding that technique-count no longer predicts actor risk suggests security teams should rethink how they classify and monitor AI-assisted threat actors, though the full scoring instrument itself is not published.
practices.quote: In the first six-month period of our analysis, 33% of actors were classified by our risk-scoring system as medium risk or higher. But by the second six-month period, that share had jumped to 56%—a roughly 1.7-fold increase.

practices.reason: The observation that MITRE ATT&CK has no ID for agentic orchestration behavior is a gap engineers evaluating AI-enabled threats should be aware of, though no replacement framework is handed over yet.
practices.quote: There is no ATT&CK ID for this type of agentic orchestration—yet these are precisely the behaviors we expect to see much more of as AI agents become more capable.
